children: and Politico covered President Donald Trump at the United Nations on Tuesday, despite being barred from the White House, as the news organizations prepared for a court hearing challenging the administration's decision, Reuters reported on Tuesday.
The reporters used press credentials issued by the UN to cover Trump's appearance at the General Assembly in New York. Trump questioned CNN's
presence as he entered the UN building, saying he was surprised the network was covering him.

The US President announced the White House restrictions on Friday, accusing the three outlets of repeatedly publishing what he described as false reports about the president. The organizations filed a lawsuit on Monday against Trump and other administration officials, arguing that the move infringed on constitutional protections for freedom of speech and the press.
They are asking a federal court in Washington, D.C., to temporarily block the restrictions. U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly is scheduled to hear the case on Wednesday.
is among five television networks that form the primary White House TV pool, alongside ABC, CBS, Fox News
had been due to provide the pool feed for Trump's UN trip but was unable to do so, leading the other networks to suspend presidential pool coverage.
The White House responded by launching a “Trump TV” stream featuring videos and highlights of the administration's achievements.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday that the outlets were not banned but were no longer permitted to work from the White House workspace.

title: Media outlets barred by Trump cover his UN appearance
